message.content:
Below is a concise summary of the most important Texas traffic‑law provisions you’ll encounter as a driver, rider, or passenger. For full legal texts consult the **Texas Transportation Code** (available online at https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/txcode/TTC.htm) or your local county clerk’s office. | Area | Key Statute / Section | Practical Takeaway | |------|-----------------------|--------------------| | **Speed Limits** | §545.001 – General Speed Limit Rules
§545.002 – Posted Speed Limits
§545.003 – Special Conditions (e.g., construction zones) | • Minimum posted limit is 35 mph.
• In rural areas, speeds may rise up to 75 mph where posted.
• Always obey posted signs—speed limits change with road type, weather, and visibility. | | **Seat Belt & Child Restraint Laws** | §545.021 – Seat Belts
§545.022 – Children Under Six Years Old Must Be Secured | • All occupants must wear belts unless exempted (medical).
• Children under six must ride rear‑seat child safety seats. | | **DUI/DWI Regulations** | §542.011 – Alcoholic Beverage Control Act (BAC limits)
§542.015 – Penalties for Driving While Intoxicated | • BAC ≥0.08% triggers DWI charges.
• Zero tolerance applies to drivers under 21 (any detectable alcohol).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, mandatory education programs, and possible jail time. | | **Texting & Phone Use** | §545.031 – Cellphone Use Restrictions | • Hands‑free devices allowed only when operating a motor vehicle.
• Texting while driving is prohibited except via hands‑free mode. | | **Right‑of‑Way & Intersection Rules** | §§545.041–545.045 | • Yield rules vary by intersection type (stop sign vs. yield sign).
• “Give way” means stop before entering the intersection until it’s safe. | | **School Bus Stop Sign Law** | §545.051 | • Drivers must stop within 20 feet of a school bus displaying its stop sign.
• Failure results in a $500 fine plus potential license revocation. | | **Pedestrian Safety** | §545.061 – Pedestrians Have Right-of-Way | • Vehicles must yield to pedestrians crossing marked crosswalks or unmarked intersections. | | **Lane Discipline** | §545.071 – Lane Usage Requirements | • Keep right lane unless passing or turning left.
• Improper lane changes can lead to citations. | | **Parking Violations** | §545.081 – Parking Rules | • No parking in fire lanes, handicap spaces without proper permits, or near driveways. | | **Vehicle Equipment Standards** | §545.091 – Vehicle Inspection & Emissions | • Required equipment includes working headlights, taillights, turn signals, brakes, mirrors, horn, and valid registration plates. | ### Enforcement Tips 1. **Keep Documentation Handy:** Registration, insurance card, and proof of inspection stickers visible inside the car. 2. **Know Your Local County Ordinances:** Some counties add extra restrictions (e.g., stricter speed limits on highways). 3. **Use Official Apps:** Texas Department of Public Safety offers mobile apps for checking ticket status and payment options. 4. **Avoid Distractions:** Even brief phone calls or text messages increase risk of accidents—and tickets. --- #### Quick Reference Links * [Texas Transportation Code](https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/txcode/TTC.htm) * [TXDOT Traffic Safety Statistics](http://www.txdot.state.tx.us/) * [Department of Motor Vehicles – Driver Handbook](https://dmv.org/handbook) Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper details on any section, such as penalty calculations, court procedures, or how new legislation might affect existing rules!
